finding: The Overview still ships the cut mechanism as a deliverable, and it is the paragraph a decomposer reads first. §1 lines 20-24: '**Two deliverables, and only the first is a no-op by default.** §2 ships `audit_converge_on` ... and changes nothing for a project that does not set it. §3 changes `consecutive_clean` and `converged` for **any** project whose spec moves between rounds, opted in or not. An earlier draft of this paragraph claimed the whole release was behaviour-preserving; it is not, and §3 is why.' §3 is now titled 'What this release deliberately does not contain' and its whole content is the record of the spec-hash reset being cut to `spec/0.46.0.md` §8.4. So every clause of that paragraph is false after the cut: there is one deliverable, not two; §3 changes nothing for any project; and the release IS behaviour-preserving by default, which is the strongest thing §2 has to say for itself. The damage is not cosmetic: §1 is what an implementer or a decomposer reads to size the release, and this paragraph directs a task to be created for a mechanism the release deliberately does not contain — the exact re-proposal §3 says it was written to prevent ('the next reader will otherwise re-propose it'). §1 was not in this round's MODIFIED list, which is why the cut passed it by.
suggestion: Rewrite the paragraph to the post-cut truth: 'One deliverable, and it is a no-op by default. §2 ships `audit_converge_on` — its resolution, its fence, its validation and its documentation — and changes nothing for a project that does not set it. The release is behaviour-preserving until an operator opts in; §3 records the one mechanism that was cut to keep it so.' Then re-read §1's opening two paragraphs for the same reason — the header note and the 93%-advisory measurement still read as the motivation for a two-part release.

finding: §4 carries three cross-references that no longer resolve to what they name, and one of them points at a test that does not exist. (1) Non-Goal 4: '`review_converge_on` is unchanged. **§3 adds a function rather than altering the shared one** precisely so review's `--status` cannot move.' §3 adds no function — it is now the record of what was cut — so the stated reason review's `--status` cannot move is gone, and a reader checking the non-goal finds its argument missing rather than merely restated. (2) The reversed-guard paragraph: `:498`'s streak-entry assertion is described as one '**which §3's reset touches**'. There is no §3 reset; nothing in this release touches that assertion, which removes the only reason §4 gives for naming it among the three a unit might delete. (3) The same paragraph ends '**§5 test 12** pins all nine.' §5 is numbered 1-11; there is no test 12. The test that pins the nine is test 11 ('The nine surviving assertions of `TestAuditGate_NoEscapeHatchFromTheGate` still pass, including `:498`'s streak-entry shape'). The off-by-one is the cut's fingerprint: §5 lost a test when §3 went, and the reference was not renumbered with it. These are checkable mechanically — a §-reference and a 'test N' reference can both be resolved against the file's own headings and list numbering — which is why they should not be surviving a sixth round by prose reading.
suggestion: (1) Rewrite Non-Goal 4 to the surviving reason: '`review_converge_on` is unchanged. This release adds an audit-side predicate and alters no shared function, so review's `--status` cannot move.' (2) Delete 'and which §3's reset touches', or replace it with the reason `:498` is still worth naming — `spec/0.34.0.tasks.json` records it as this file's mutation-killing assertion, which stands on its own. (3) '§5 test 12' → 'test 11'. Then sweep the whole file for `§3`, `§5 test <n>` and `spec/0.46.0.md §8*` targets and resolve each against the current headings and list numbering; this round's cut moved all three coordinate systems at once.

finding: §2.2's closing sentence points at the wrong test, and the test it names says the opposite of what §2.2 needs. §2.2: '§5 **test 5** uses a legacy row because it is convenient and real, not because the case is live.' §5 test 5 is '**`warning` is advisory**, tested separately from `info` because `warning` is 158 of the corpus's 360 non-`PASS` rows' — it uses no legacy row and has nothing to do with out-of-enum severities. The test §2.2 means is **test 7** ('Unrecognised fails closed ... three fixtures, because a legacy row supplies only (a): all 67 carry a present, non-null `high`/`medium`/`low`'), which is the only place in §5 a legacy row appears. Verified against the corpus that the surrounding numbers are right — 67 out-of-enum rows across v0.29.0-v0.32.0 in exactly 15 files as `high` 16 / `medium` 15 / `low` 36, 0 out-of-enum in 238 non-`PASS` rows across v0.33.0-v0.36.0, `warning` 158 of 360 — so the defect is the pointer alone, which is what makes it worth fixing rather than re-deriving: everything around it is sound and one wrong digit sends the reader to a test that contradicts the paragraph citing it.
suggestion: '§5 test 5' → '§5 test 7'. Same renumbering sweep as §4's 'test 12': §5 was renumbered when the cut removed its tests and the references into it were not moved.

finding: Non-Goal 6 defers a deliverable on a premise §2 falsifies four paragraphs earlier, and the shipped surface agrees with §2. Non-Goal 6: 'Under `blocking`, a clean round can have surviving `warning` and `info` rows and **tp emits no count of them**, so an agent reading `clean: true` cannot tell an empty round from a suppressed one.' §2's boundary paragraph says the opposite in terms: '`role_streaks[].open` ... computed by `auditRoundOpenByRole` (`engine/rolestreaks.go:128-142`) through `AuditRowIsPass` alone. Under `blocking` a round can therefore record `clean: true` beside a **non-zero `open`** — correct rather than defective: `open` counts findings, `clean` answers whether the phase may end.' Verified in the shipped surface rather than inferred: `skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:758-796` documents `role_streaks` as emitted on `tp audit <spec> --status` (with or without `--check`) and on `tp audit <spec> --record <file>`, each entry `{role, consecutive_clean, open}`, and `internal/cli/audit_record.go:152` sets it unconditionally as an always-emitted array. So under `blocking` an agent reading `clean: true` sees `role_streaks` and the sum of `open` over it is exactly the count of suppressed rows: zero for an empty round, non-zero for a suppressed one. The two cases are distinguishable today, in JSON, without reading round files. What is genuinely missing is the *severity breakdown* — how many of the surviving rows are `warning` versus `info` — which is a much smaller deferral than 'no count' and does not support Non-Goal 6's closing instruction ('an operator setting `blocking` reads the round files for what was suppressed'), since `--status` already answers how many. This matters beyond wording: the false premise is being handed forward — `spec/0.46.0.md` §8.3 receives this non-goal, so the spec that is supposed to build the counterpart will start from a claim that tp emits nothing.
suggestion: Restate Non-Goal 6 on the true gap: 'Under `blocking`, a clean round can carry surviving `warning` and `info` rows. Their *count* is already observable — `role_streaks[].open` stays severity-blind by §2's boundary, so a non-zero `open` beside `clean: true` is exactly the suppressed population — but their *severity breakdown* is not, and `nonblocking_open`'s review-side shape is what would give it. Creating the counterpart means inverting a pinned guard, which this release does not do.' Delete 'reads the round files for what was suppressed' and put `role_streaks[].open` there instead. Correct `spec/0.46.0.md` §8.3 in the same edit, since it already carries the inherited version of this claim.

finding: §2 bans a word in the sentence immediately below the table that uses it, and the banned word is in the normative definition of one of the two values. The table (line 46): '| `all` | no non-`PASS` row **survives**, whatever its severity |'. The very next paragraph (lines 49-50): 'Both predicates are over the round's non-`PASS` rows. **"Surviving" is deliberately not the word:** it would imply a disposition that removes a row from the count, which Non-Goal 2 declines to create.' Read literally, the release's own reasoning says the `all` row implies a disposition mechanism Non-Goal 2 explicitly refuses to build — so the normative statement of the default predicate references a mechanism the release does not have, and the disclaimer that was added to fix the `blocking` row now indicts the row beside it. The word also survives in two further places the disclaimer governs: §5 test 4 ('a round with one **surviving** `info` row is not clean') and §4 Non-Goal 6 ('a clean round can have **surviving** `warning` and `info` rows'). This is the same class an earlier round reported against the `blocking` row; the repair corrected that row and added the prose rule without applying the rule to its three siblings, so an implementer now has a stated rule and three counterexamples to it in the same file, and no way to tell which is normative.
suggestion: Make the table match the rule the paragraph states: '| `all` | no non-`PASS` row is recorded in the round, whatever its severity |' — the same shape as the `blocking` row's 'no non-`PASS` row in the round carries a blocking severity'. Apply it to test 4 ('a round with one `info` row is not clean') and Non-Goal 6 ('a clean round can have `warning` and `info` rows recorded in it'). Since the rule is now stated normatively, it is also mechanizable: a `workflow.checks` entry grepping this file for `surviv` outside the disclaimer sentence would keep the fourth instance from arriving.

finding: §2.1's second row measures a cycle that has not finished, and §5 test 8 freezes that unfinished history into testdata under a rationale that rules out exactly this. §2.1: '| v0.36.0 | **13, never converged** | round 3 (r2, r3 carry zero `error`) | **never — no round reaches zero** |'. Read from the corpus: `spec/.tp-review/0.36.0/state.json` holds 13 audit rounds, the last recorded 2026-09-01T19:37:28Z with 3 non-`PASS` rows (2 `error`, 1 `warning`) and `clean: false`, and CLAUDE.md's release table lists v0.36.0 as **In flight**. So 'never converged' and 'never — no round reaches zero' are statements about a loop that is still running: a round 14 is expected, and the cycle converging under `all` at rounds 14-15 would falsify both cells. §5 test 8 then pins them — '`blocking` at 3 and `all` never for the second. Both rows are pinned because the v0.36.0 row is the one that argues against the default' — while its own justification for using testdata is 'that is live state **for cycles still in flight**, and an acceptance criterion that moves when unrelated work is recorded is not one.' Copying an in-flight history into `testdata/` does not satisfy that rationale, it evades it: the criterion stops moving but starts being wrong, and it is wrong about the cycle §2.1 calls decisive. Everything else in §2.1 checks out against the corpus — v0.35.0 converges under `blocking` at 3 and under `all` at 9, round 4 carries {error 1, warning 2, info 1}, v0.36.0's rounds 7, 12 and 13 each carry `error`, and the round-3 cell is right for both — which is why the in-flight cells are the only thing to fix.
suggestion: Two options, both honest. (a) Cite the v0.36.0 row as of a stated round and commit — '| v0.36.0 | 13 rounds recorded at <sha>, not converged | round 3 | not by round 13 |' — and make test 8 assert the same bounded claim ('`all` does not converge within the 13 recorded rounds'), which stays true however the cycle ends. (b) Wait for v0.36.0 to close before pinning it, since this release already depends on v0.36.0 shipping elsewhere in the plan. Do not leave 'never' in either the table or the test: it is the one word the cycle can still refute, and it is load-bearing for the default.

finding: The release widens a shipped closed enum and enumerates none of the surfaces that state it, in a file that enumerates four places for `nonblocking_open` and two for the five-layer chain. §2: '`--decision` is a closed, validated enum (`skip-gate, raise-review-cap, raise-audit-cap, import-force, other` — **`escalate.go:41`**, enforced by `IsEscalationDecision`) ... **This release adds `audit-converge-on` to that enum** and maps the field to it.' Two problems, both checked. (1) The citation points at prose, not the definition. `internal/cli/escalate.go:41-42` is inside the command's `Long` help string ('--decision is one of skip-gate, raise-review-cap, raise-audit-cap, import-force or other'), hardcoded rather than built from `engine.EscalationDecisions()` — unlike the flag usage at :52 and the refusal hint at :85, which are. The definition is `internal/engine/escalation.go:21-37`. So the one line §2 cites is a surface that must be hand-edited, and the spec cites it as if it were the source. (2) The five are restated verbatim in at least five more places no line of this release names: `engine/escalation.go:19-20` ('a decision outside it is a usage error, **not a sixth category**' — a comment this release makes false), `:39` ('returns the five documented decisions'), `:47` ('reports whether decision is one of **the five**'), `skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:347`, and `skills/tp/SKILL.md:247` plus `:372`. `spec/0.35.0.md:429` states the closed set as a shipped clause. §2's cost paragraph puts REFERENCE.md and SKILL.md in scope generically, which is not the same as naming the rows, and the code comments are in no list at all. The asymmetry is the finding: this release's method everywhere else is to count and name the surfaces before touching them, and the one enum it actually mutates got neither.
suggestion: Name them the way §2 names the five-layer sweep: 'The enum is `engine/escalation.go:21-37`; adding a sixth value also touches `escalate.go:41-42` (the `Long` help hardcodes the five rather than building them from `EscalationDecisions()`), three comments in `escalation.go` that say "the five" and "not a sixth category" (:19-20, :39, :47), `skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:347` and `skills/tp/SKILL.md:247` and `:372`.' Consider making `escalate.go`'s `Long` derive from `EscalationDecisions()` in the same task, so the next value costs one edit instead of seven — but say so explicitly, since it is a change to a shipped help surface.

finding: §5's closing paragraph is an exhaustiveness claim about what the release leaves untested, and it names one omission out of several. '**What is not tested here, named so its absence is deliberate.** `clean` is this release's only gated surface; `role_streaks[].open` and `spec_coverage_clean_rounds` stay severity-blind by §2's stated boundary.' §2 declares documentation work as release scope in four separate places and §5 has no test, and no `workflow.checks` entry, for any of it: (a) '**it still stands in two other places this release must sweep**: `skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:519-522` ... and `spec/0.31.0.md:41`'; (b) '`REFERENCE.md:327-328` additionally names `TP_RUN_MAX_UNITS` and `TP_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS`, neither of which exists in any non-test source'; (c) the escalation-enum widening, whose doc surfaces §2 does not enumerate at all; (d) §4's own admission that the inflated `nonblocking_open` count 'was copied into `spec/0.46.0.md` before anyone checked it' — verified still live, `spec/0.46.0.md:330` reads 'six places pin its **absence** on the audit side'. Of the eleven tests, tests 1-11 cover the field, the fence, the enum's behaviour and the replay; none reaches a documentation string. So the release's stated scope and its acceptance criteria diverge, and the paragraph that would surface the divergence asserts the opposite. The direction matters: v0.31.1 exists as a whole release because v0.31.0 shipped the twin with two surfaces missing, which §2 itself cites as the reason test 3 exists — the same failure mode is open here on four doc surfaces instead of two command surfaces.
suggestion: Either extend the closing paragraph to name the doc sweeps as untested-on-purpose and say what makes them acceptable, or add the check that makes them testable. The second is cheap and this repository's own rule prefers it: one `workflow.checks` entry grepping the tree for `CLI > env > task override` and for `TP_RUN_MAX_UNITS`/`TP_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` outside `spec/.tp-review/` turns three of the four into a red/green signal, and the fourth (`spec/0.46.0.md:330`) is a one-line edit that should be named in §2's sweep list rather than only confessed in §4.

finding: The header note describes a repair that this round partly reversed, and states a file size that is no longer this file's. The note (lines 3-8): 'The prose recording which drafts were withdrawn is gone with them: it had grown to **77 of the file's 306 lines**, which is `spec/0.43.0.md` §2's repair-verbosity class measured on this file.' Two things are now off. (1) The file is **265 lines**, not 306, and the sentence states the number with a present possessive ('the file's 306 lines') rather than as a measurement of the pre-rewrite draft — the exact shape CLAUDE.md's 'a measured constant in a comment goes stale faster than a release' names. (2) §3, added this round, is 29 lines of prose recording which drafts were withdrawn, round by round, with a three-row table of the classes that falsified them — the genre the note says is 'gone with them'. §3 earns its place (it stops the mechanism being re-proposed, which is its stated purpose) but the header now reads as a rule the very next section breaks, and a later reader following the header will delete §3 as repair verbosity. This is the cheapest finding in the file and the one most likely to survive another round unread, because nothing in §5 or `workflow.checks` measures a line count.
suggestion: Rewrite as a bounded past measurement and reconcile it with §3: 'The prose recording which drafts were withdrawn is gone from §2: at round 3 it had grown to 77 of that draft's 306 lines, which is `spec/0.43.0.md` §2's repair-verbosity class measured on this file. §3 keeps 29 lines of it deliberately, for the one mechanism that was cut rather than repaired — the record is what stops it being re-proposed.' Either drop the raw counts or tie them to the round and draft they measured; do not restate the current file's length in prose, since nothing keeps it honest.

finding: Four near-misses, caught by counting rather than by reading. (1) I was going to file that §1's, §2.1's and §2.2's measurements had drifted, since three of the six rounds so far have turned on a miscounted figure. I recomputed every one from `spec/.tp-review/*/audit-round-*.ndjson` and **all of them are exact**: v0.35.0's nine rounds hold 42 non-`PASS` rows as 3 `error` / 22 `warning` / 17 `info` (93% advisory); under `audit_clean_rounds: 2` v0.35.0 converges at round 3 under `blocking` and round 9 under `all`, and v0.36.0 at round 3 under `blocking` and never through round 13 under `all`; v0.35.0's round 4 is {error 1, warning 2, info 1}; v0.36.0's rounds 7, 12 and 13 each carry `error`; the legacy set is 67 rows in exactly 15 files as `high` 16 / `medium` 15 / `low` 36; v0.33.0-v0.36.0 hold 238 non-`PASS` rows with **zero** out-of-enum severities; and `warning` is 158 of the corpus's 360 non-`PASS` rows. The numbers are the strongest part of this draft and should not be re-derived a seventh time. (2) I was going to file that §3's table cites class slugs that were never recorded. All three resolve: `mechanism-falsifies-its-own-replay` is in `review-round-3.ndjson`, `prospectivity-without-a-marker` in round 4, `prospectivity-marker-does-not-discriminate` in round 5. (3) I was going to file that widening the `--decision` enum reverses a second shipped test guard, falsifying §4's 'One shipped guard is deliberately reversed'. It does not: `escalate_test.go:158` iterates the five as *valid* inputs (a sixth value leaves every arm green), `unattended_fence_test.go:102` asserts `Contains(... "raise-audit-cap")`, and v0.34.2's command-surface baseline pins `escalate: decision evidence option` — flag names, not values. No test turns red, so the 'one guard' claim stands and the enum finding is correctly scoped to documentation. (4) The file is 265 newline-terminated lines by `wc -l`; the round-6 prompt tp emitted says '266 lines'. The difference is the trailing newline, not a drift — recorded so the line-count finding is not itself refuted by tp's own header.
suggestion: No spec change. If the numeric block is ever moved or re-stated, move it whole: it is the one part of this file that has survived six rounds unfalsified, and every attempt to paraphrase a figure in this cycle has introduced an error.
